regime_context: Canada/TSX detector shows broad but shallow rotation (9 of 16 eligible, absorption 0.33, not one-narrative). Oil & Gas leads on rank but with weak durability (0.5 bar, mixed Hurst, low 0.357 breadth); Consumer Staples & Big Banks show the strongest durability/breadth legs (0.81 and 0.8 bars, full 1.0 breadth, 'trend' Hurst). Track record shows 55.8% hit rate but only 31.3% directional accuracy — the calls mostly avoid tails rather than pick winners, so conviction should be low.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Consumer Staples & Retail confirms a handoff from Oil & Gas as the leader: the observable condition is XST.TO closing above XEG.TO on a 10-day relative basis while Oil & Gas durability_bar (currently 0.5) drifts below 0.4. Until that happens, Oil & Gas remains the leader with weak breadth and I treat the Staples lead as co-leadership, not a rotation.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the strongest trend-discipline leg in the eligible set: eligible=true, durability_bar 0.8, Hurst 'trend', breadth 1.0 (all constituents participating), crowding_z modest at 0.75 (not crowded). Under the detector's only validated edge — the absolute-trend gate for drawdown/shake-out avoidance — this is the cleanest stay-in-trend candidate among scorable themes. Rank is #3, which I treat as a focus lens only; the lean rests on the trend-gate + breadth/durability texture, not on the rank.
evidence: durability_bar 0.80, Hurst 'trend', breadth 1.0 (the strongest trend-health combo in the eligible set)
theses.dissent: Financials are rate- and credit-cycle sensitive; the macro backdrop shows inflation and geopolitics (US-Iran war headline) as active narratives, and an unscheduled-surprise share of 0.68 means headline shocks could hit bank spreads or loan books fast. A trend that looks broad today can crack on a single macro event.

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: Consumer Staples & Retail has the single highest durability_bar (0.81) and full breadth (1.0) among all 16 themes, with Hurst 'trend' and eligible=true. In a macro tape dominated by geopolitics and inflation headlines, a defensive-staples trend with full constituent participation is a reasonable stay-in-theme lean under the trend-gate discipline. Rank #2 is context only, not the basis.
evidence: durability_bar 0.81, full breadth 1.0, Hurst 'trend' (strongest durability texture in the table)
theses.dissent: Staples leadership is often a late-cycle/defensive signal — if the AI-tech macro theme re-accelerates risk appetite, defensive flows could rotate out quickly. Also, the rotation gap to Oil & Gas is narrow (0.118 margin), so this is not a confirmed handoff, just a co-leader with better durability texture.

falsifier.text: XST.TO underperforms ZEB.TO by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology is the only crowded theme (crowded=true, crowding_z 1.25) in an eligible-but-mixed state (eligibility true but Hurst 'mixed', score negative at -0.06). The crowding flag is a size-down caution only — never a fade or short — and the guardrails explicitly warn not to treat attention/spike as a buy. With the macro narrative dominated by ai_tech headlines (7 of 19) and an unscheduled-share of 0.68, the crowding flag plus heavy attention makes this a stay-away rather than a lean.
evidence: guardrails: do not treat attention spikes as a buy
theses.dissent: The macro narrative IS ai_tech — if the fundamental cycle is real, crowding can persist and the theme can keep working despite the flag. Avoiding crowded winners is a documented way to miss the strongest trends.
